subject.title: Memory compaction blocks main processing lane, causing unresponsive bot for 10+ minutes

question: Should OpenClaw isolate memory flush and preflight compaction from foreground reply admission for #53008, and should that isolation be a dedicated maintenance lane, background compaction, or a bounded foreground-recovery policy?
rationale: The source-reproducible bug is real, but the repair changes session scheduling, transcript rotation, active-run admission, and channel acknowledgment semantics that need maintainer ownership before automation is safe.

options.title: Dedicated Maintenance Lane
options.body: Move memory flush and eligible preflight compaction to a bounded maintenance lane while keeping session transcript rotation guarded by explicit ordering tests.

options.title: Bound Foreground Recovery
options.body: Keep compaction in the foreground path but add stricter abort, user notice, and stale-operation recovery so queued messages resume quickly after maintenance stalls.

options.title: Fold Into Lifecycle Umbrella
options.body: Track this only through #101863 and close #53008 later once the broader run-lifecycle design proves the compaction-lane user flow.

recommendation.title: Dedicated Maintenance Lane
recommendation.body: Move memory flush and eligible preflight compaction to a bounded maintenance lane while keeping session transcript rotation guarded by explicit ordering tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest sampled owner for the memory-flush and reply-runner surface, while broader lifecycle choices can be coordinated with #101863.
